content.thinking:
"distinct owners 26" — because `longname(i)` only depends on `i % 26`! So all 66 CNAME owners are the same 26 names repeated → each owner has multiple CNAME records with *different* targets → "exactly one distinct target" violated → invalid. My test data generator bug. Let me make the names actually distinct by varying the last label.

Let me use labels: 126 labels of 'a' plus one varying label at the end.

wire = 126*2 + (1+len(lbl)) + 1. With lbl of 1 char: 252+2+1 = 255. ✓

So: labels = ['a']*126 + [chr(ord('a') + (i%26))] → 127 labels, wire 255. And to make targets distinct, vary the last label.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp/t && sed -i "s|    labels = \[chr(ord('a') + (i % 26))\] \* 127|    labels = ['a'] * 126 + [chr(ord('a') + (i % 26)) + 'x']|" stress.py && sed -i "s|    return '.'.join(labels) + '.'|    return '.'.join(labels) + '.'|" stress.py && python3 -c "
import re
s=open('stress.py').read()
s=s.replace(\"labels = ['a'] * 126 + [chr(ord('a') + (i % 26)) + 'x']\", \"labels = ['a'] * 126 + [chr(ord('a') + (i % 26))]\")
open('stress.py','w').write(s)
" && python3 stress.py
